        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **zelarhq/nodejs-welcome** repository.  
I’ve written the files in plain text so you can copy‑paste them into your editor, then run the git commands that follow.

> **NOTE** – I can’t actually clone or push to the repo from here, but the commands below will work once you’re on your machine.

---

## 1. Clone the repo

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2. Analyse & Add the following files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – Node 18 (LTS) on Alpine for a small footprint
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install app dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Bundle app source
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why Node 18?*  
> The repo’s `package.json` (look at the `engines` field or the `node` version used in CI) shows it works with Node 18.  
> If you see a different version in `package.json`, replace `node:18-alpine` with that version.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes manifests

Create a folder `k8s` (or keep them in the root – whichever you prefer).  
I’ll put both the Deployment and Service in a single file for brevity.

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Replace** `<YOUR_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>` with your Docker Hub account name.  
> If you’re using a private registry, change the `image:` line accordingly (e.g. `registry.example.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`).

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create the file `.github/workflows/docker-image.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docker-image.yml
name: Build & Push Docker image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Docker Buildx
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      # Log in to Docker Hub
      - name: Login to DockerHub
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build and push the image
      - name: Build & push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v3
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Secrets**  
> In the GitHub repo settings → *Secrets → Actions*, add:
> * `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username  
> * `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` – a Docker Hub access token (or password)

---

## 3. Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-image.yml
```

> If you kept the Kubernetes files in the root, adjust the path accordingly.

---

## 4. Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and GitHub Actions workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run, build the Docker image, and push it to Docker Hub.

---

## 5. Verify

1. **Docker image** – Check Docker Hub to confirm the `nodejs-welcome:latest` image exists.  
2. **Kubernetes** – If you have a cluster, apply the manifests:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
   ```

   Then verify:

   ```bash
   kubectl get pods
   kubectl get svc
   ```

3. **Local test** – Build locally to double‑check everything works:

   ```bash
   docker build -t nodejs-welcome:local .
   docker run -p 3000:3000 nodejs-welcome:local
   ```

   Visit `http://localhost:3000` to see the app.

---

### Quick Recap of the Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node image. |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys 2 replicas, exposes port 3000. |
| `k8s/service.yaml` (inside same file) | ClusterIP service mapping port 80 → 3000. |
| `.github/workflows/docker-image.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes Docker image on pushes to `main`. |

Feel free to tweak the Docker image tag, replica count, or service type (e.g. `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer`) to match your environment. Happy coding!
